name: Exact Width for Nested-Section Substitution
statement: Let $\emptyset\ne B\subseteq A$, let $F$ be proper and nonempty, and assume $F^{\mathrm c}$ is dismantlable ample. Then $\sigma((A\times F)\cup(B\times\{0,1\}^Y);A\times F)=\max\{\sigma(A),\sigma(B),\sigma(F)\}$. If $B\subsetneq A$, the same formula holds for absolute width; if $A=B$, the output is $A\times\{0,1\}^Y$ and has width $\sigma(A)$. Consequently, substituting a test with two dismantlable sides preserves the absolute width of every outer class with nested sections.
proof: Reverse complement filling gives $\sigma_{\square}(F)=\sigma(F)$, and the exact one-stage rectangular-extension formula gives the prescribed equality. When $B\subsetneq A$, conditioning an exclusive outer word recovers $F$, while conditioning inner words on the two test sides recovers $A$ and $B$, so the same maximum is a lower bound for absolute width. The width of the original nested two-section outer class is already $\max\{\sigma(A),\sigma(B)\}$, proving preservation when both test sides have width zero.
comments: Empty smaller sections reduce to products, and reflecting the substituted bit handles the opposite nesting direction. No isometry assumption is used.
